analysis.investment_thesis: Ahluwalia Contracts is a clean-balance-sheet EPC stalwart riding India's infrastructure capex cycle with 14% revenue CAGR and near-zero debt (D/E 0.04), but razor-thin 6.6% operating margins and cyclical earnings dynamics cap its upside at a forward P/E of 17x. This is a decent stalwart, not the ten-bagger I'm hunting for.
key_strengths: Pristine balance sheet — borrowings of just INR 76 Cr against equity of INR 1,924 Cr (D/E 0.04) with INR 318 Cr cash gives it crisis resilience rare in EPC
Consistent OCF generation — 5/5 years positive, INR 359 Cr in FY2025, confirming real earnings and not accounting mirages
India infrastructure tailwind — government + PSU revenue mix means a visible multi-year order pipeline as India's capex supercycle continues
key_risks: Margin compression risk — operating income actually fell from INR 388 Cr to INR 342 Cr in FY2025 even as revenue grew 6.3% to INR 4,099 Cr; margins are thin and deteriorating
Earnings quality concern — FY2024 net profit of INR 375 Cr included INR 232 Cr other income (vs. typical ~30 Cr), masking that normalized earnings are only ~INR 175–200 Cr
Capex escalation — investing CF surged to -INR 323 Cr in FY2025 (from -INR 46 Cr in FY2020), squeezing FCF to just INR 171 Cr (~3% FCF yield on market cap)
red_flags: FY2024 other income of INR 232 Cr (vs. FY2023: INR 30 Cr) inflated net profit to INR 375 Cr — the FY2025 collapse to INR 202 Cr exposes how weak core earnings power really is
Operating margin of 6.59% leaves almost no room for error on project execution, cost overruns, or commodity inflation — a single bad quarter can wipe the year
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Ahluwalia Contracts is what I'd classify as a stalwart-cyclical — a solid, well-managed construction company growing steadily but not explosively. Revenue CAGR of 14.1% over 9 years is respectable, but this is a business where the earnings story is messy. The PEG looks appealing at first glance: forward P/E of 17x against ~15–18% expected growth implies a PEG of roughly 0.9–1.1. That's okay, but not the below-0.8 PEG I get excited about. More importantly, the 9-year net profit CAGR of only 10.2% tells me operating leverage is weak, and FY2025's INR 202 Cr earnings on INR 4,099 Cr revenue (net margin ~5%) is not the profile of a compounder.

The bull case rests on India's infrastructure boom — the company serves government, PSU, and private developers across hospitals, IT parks, metro stations, and data centers, which is exactly the sectors growing fast. The near-zero debt gives it staying power through cycles. But the ROE of 11.9% barely clears my 12% threshold, the operating margin has been stuck in a narrow band and is now slipping, and increasing capex (-INR 189 Cr in FY2025) is consuming cash that could otherwise compound equity. At INR 834, the stock is fairly valued for what it is — a dependable mid-size contractor — but I need to see margin expansion or a re-rating catalyst to get more excited. I'd watch for order book growth and margin recovery before building a position.
